title: The teen numbers
keyIdea: Teen numbers from 11 to 19 are one full ten and some leftover ones. Fourteen is a ten-frame filled plus four more: 10 + 4. Seventeen is 10 + 7. Seeing teens this way is early place value: the 1 in 14 stands for one ten, and the 4 stands for four ones.

kid: Teen numbers go from 11 to 19. Each one is a full ten and some more ones.
Fill a ten-frame. That is one ten. Then put leftover ones beside it. Ten and four is fourteen.
You can also split a teen. Start with 14 ones, pull out a ten, and count 4 left. So 14 = 10 + 4.
The first digit in 14 means one ten. The second digit means four ones.
adult: Kindergarten and Year 1 place value ask children to compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones (CCSS K.NBT.1, 1.NBT.2.b; early NC place value). Keep the language concrete: ten-frame, leftover ones, 10 + n.

Words to use: teen, ten-frame, ten, ones, leftover, compose, decompose, 10 + 4 = 14. Common mistakes: counting only the leftover ones and saying 14 is 4; reading digits backwards (41); thinking 11 is two separate ones with no ten; calling 10 itself a teen.
In the lab your child fills a ten-frame, adds leftover ones, reads teens as 10 + n, splits 14 into ten and ones, and builds 16.

familyTip: Use an egg box cut to ten holes, or draw a ten-frame on paper. Make 14 with ten in the frame and four beside it. Say 'ten and four' before you say 'fourteen'.

practice.hint: Keep one full ten, then count the leftover ones.
practice.explain: Fourteen is one ten and four ones, written 10 + 4.

choices: one full ten and some ones
practice.explain: Every teen has exactly one ten plus some leftover ones.

practice.hint: Start at ten, then count on seven ones.
practice.explain: Ten and seven ones make seventeen.

practice.prompt: One ten and {n} ones make what number?
practice.hint: Add the leftover ones on to the full ten to find the teen total.
practice.explain: One ten plus {n} ones makes the teen number {=10+n}.

practice.prompt: {n} is a teen. How many ones are left after you pull out one ten?
practice.hint: Take 10 away from the teen number.

pool.hint: Teen numbers are the numbers from 11 up to 19 only.
pool.explain: 13 is between 11 and 19. 30 is three tens. 3 is just ones.

pool.hint: Pull out the ten; count what remains.
pool.explain: 19 is one ten and nine ones, so 19 = 10 + 9.

choices: it looks like two 1s side by side
pool.hint: Think of eleven as one full ten and one leftover one.
pool.explain: 11 is one ten and one one. Looking like two 1s is about digits, not value.

pool.hint: Teens need leftover ones from 1 to 9.
pool.explain: 10 is one ten and zero ones. Teens start at 11.

pool.prompt: Sam counts only the four leftover ones and says the number is 4. The ten-frame is full. What did Sam miss?
choices: the full ten, so it is 14
pool.hint: A full ten-frame is worth ten, not one.
pool.explain: The full frame is one ten. Ten and four is fourteen.

pool.hint: A teen has exactly one ten, then some leftover ones beside it.

pool.prompt: One ten and {n} ones. What total?
pool.hint: Start from ten, then count on the leftover ones to get the total.
pool.explain: One ten and {n} ones make the teen {=10+n}.

pool.prompt: You have {n}. Pull out one ten. How many ones remain?
pool.explain: After you pull one ten out of {n}, {=n-10} ones remain.
